subject: Decision log: Private CP identity integration approach (SAML vs IdP-proxy + SCIM provisioning)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Katie Morrison <katie@acme-corp.com>, infra-team@acme-corp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Decision log: Private CP identity integration approach (SAML vs IdP-proxy + SCIM provisioning)

Hi Katie / Acme infra team —

Thanks again for the discovery call yesterday. Per follow-up, I wanted to capture the options we discussed for connecting your IdP to the Redwood Private control plane in your VPC and get a picture of constraints so we can land on an approach. High-level options: 

1) Direct SAML federation to Private CP control-plane endpoints (customer IdP -> Private CP SAML)
2) IdP-proxy model (customer IdP -> Acme-managed IdP-proxy / assertion broker -> Private CP)
3) Lightweight SAML for auth + SCIM for provisioning (SCIM service account handles group->role mappings)

Open questions (please confirm):
- Network egress: can the Private CP control plane reach acme-idp.acme-corp.com over TLS from the VPC control plane subnets? If not, option 2 may be required.
- SCIM provisioning: can we create a dedicated SCIM service account (scim@acme-corp.com) with token rotation via your secrets manager?
- Operator entitlements: we proposed a small set of operator roles (OperatorRead, OperatorAdmin, AuditOnly). Do these map to AD groups you already maintain?

I attached a short options matrix and a draft role-mapping CSV. Our recommended default for risk-managed customers is: SAML assertions for runtime auth + SCIM provisioning for long-lived entitlements (option 3) — with short-lived SCIM tokens and restricted IP egress from the control plane. That keeps assertion latency low and gives Acme full control of group membership.

Next steps: please flag network restrictions and SCIM token policy by EOD Friday so we can finalize the integration plan and send a single runbook for your ops/elevated access review. I can host a 30-min follow-up early next week to finalize mapping.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: privcp-saml-vs-proxy-options-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), scim-provisioning-playbook.pdf (pdf), operator-access-role-mapping.csv (csv)

From: Katie Morrison <katie@acme-corp.com>

Cc: infra-team@acme-corp.com, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision log: Private CP identity integration approach (SAML vs IdP-proxy + SCIM provisioning)

Diego — thanks for the clear summary. A couple clarifications from our side before we lock anything down: 

1) Network: our VPC does NOT allow outbound 443 to arbitrary hosts from the control plane subnets today; we restrict egress to a narrow set of endpoints via NAT gateway policies. We can add acme-idp.acme-corp.com but prefer using an internal proxy if possible.

2) SCIM: We can create a dedicated SCIM service account, but our security team requires rotated credentials via HashiCorp Vault with a 7-day TTL. Is that supported in your provisioning flow?

3) Role mapping: We use Azure AD groups for entitlement. We can provide the group IDs, but we need mapping guidance for the SAML attribute vs SCIM approach.

Also, one compliance ask — can Redwood provide an audit proof of SCIM activity (who provisioned which user) to drop into our SOC 2 evidence?

Happy to jump on the proposed 30-min call. Available Mon/Tue afternoon PT.

—Katie
Katie Morrison
Director, Infrastructure | Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Katie Morrison <katie@acme-corp.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision log: Private CP identity integration approach (SAML vs IdP-proxy + SCIM provisioning)

Thanks Katie — quick answers inline below.

> 1) Network egress / proxy
We can support both patterns. If you prefer not to open direct egress, option 2 (IdP-proxy) is viable: you would host an assertion broker inside your perimeter (or use a small bastion we co-manage) and the Private CP would speak to that single endpoint. Downside: extra hop and additional operational ownership.

> 2) SCIM token rotation (Vault)
We support SCIM tokens rotated by external secrets stores. The typical pattern we recommend: create a short-lived token (7d TTL) in Vault that a small SCIM agent rotates and pushes to the Private CP bootstrap endpoint during scheduled windows. We've attached a playbook (scim-provisioning-playbook.pdf) that describes the rotation flow and webhook-based token exchange.

> 3) Role mapping
Two recommended mappings: (A) SAML assertion attribute (e.g., SAML attribute 'groups' or 'redwood_role') used at auth time to drive ephemeral role assignments; (B) SCIM-provisioned group->role mapping for persistent entitlements (e.g., OperatorAdmin). If you can provide AD group IDs, we can populate operator-access-role-mapping.csv and show the exact mapping.

> Audit proof for SCIM activity
We produce audit logs for SCIM changes (timestamp, actor, action, diff). We can surface these via your SIEM (syslog/HTTP log forwarder) and include an S3 export for SOC 2 sampling.

I'll propose a timeslot for Mon 3/18 1:30pm PT if that works for Acme. Diego — want to own the runbook update after the call?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Decision log: Private CP identity integration approach (SAML vs IdP-proxy + SCIM provisioning)

Katie / team — adding detail on IAM role model and operator access controls so you can review during your security call.

- Operator role decomposition: 
  * OperatorRead (read-only access to runtime metrics, logs)
  * OperatorAdmin (deploy, scale, restart inference pools)
  * AuditOnly (view audit logs and access reviews)

- Mapping considerations: prefer SCIM-driven group membership for persistent assignments (helps with auditing). For emergency/just-in-time tasks we support SAML assertion that includes an 'amr' style attribute to request elevated ephemeral roles (7–30 minute TTL).

- Service accounts & service-to-service auth: we recommend creating two service accounts in your tenant: scim-agent@acme-corp.com and provisioning-agent@acme-corp.com. Each will have scoped permissions in AD to read groups / rotate tokens and will be restricted by IP via your NAT policies.

- Fallback plan: if SCIM is delayed, we can seed operator users manually for a short window and audit all changes; but this requires ticketed approvals from Acme security.

I'll update the role-mapping CSV and push to the Drive folder so you can comment.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Katie Morrison <katie@acme-corp.com>, infra-team@acme-corp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision log: Private CP identity integration approach (SAML vs IdP-proxy + SCIM provisioning)

Katie — thanks for the quick feedback. Based on constraints (no direct egress from control plane today + Vault rotation requirement) and risk tolerance, proposed approach for signoff: 

Decision (proposed, please ack):
- Use IdP-proxy model for assertion routing inside Acme perimeter. Proxy will terminate SAML with your IdP and expose a single, customer-managed endpoint for Redwood Private CP to consume. This removes the need to open broad egress from control plane subnets.
- Use SCIM provisioning for group->role sync. SCIM tokens will be rotated by HashiCorp Vault with a 7-day TTL. A small, Acme-owned scim-agent will push rotated tokens to the Private CP bootstrap endpoint within a scheduled maintenance window.
- Operator accounts will map to Azure AD groups per the attached CSV; privileged actions require either (a) SCIM membership or (b) ephemeral SAML assertion with a mapped temp-role and 15-minute TTL.
- Auditability: Redwood will stream SCIM/audit logs to your SIEM (syslog) and provide an S3 exports link for SOC sampling.

Action items and schedule: 
1) Acme to provision scim-agent@acme-corp.com and provisioning-agent@acme-corp.com in Azure AD by 2029-03-18.
2) Acme to stand up IdP-proxy endpoint (or confirm a host we can peer with) by 2029-03-20.
3) Redwood to produce final runbook and cutover checklist by 2029-03-21 (will include validation steps and rollback triggers).

If this matches your constraints, reply with ACK and we'll file the change in JIRA SECURE-4127 and schedule the cutover slot.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

ACK — we agree with the proposed decision and timeline.

Notes: 
- We will create scim-agent and provisioning-agent by EOD 2029-03-18 and share group IDs.
- We'll run token rotation via Vault with 7-day TTL.
- We'll stand up IdP-proxy with a single endpoint and share the FQDN + certificate fingerprint.

Please ensure the final runbook includes the exact log forwarder config and the SCIM audit fields (actor, timestamp, action, previous_value, new_value). If you can include a short test plan with clear success/failure signals we can use during the cutover that would be helpful.

Thanks — Katie
